Vertical 9:16 advertising image, full bleed, edge to edge. No border, no device mockup, no frame within the frame.

A doorway pull-up bar mounted in an ordinary hallway doorframe, seen slightly from below. A winter coat and a tote bag hang from it. A visible film of dust sits along the top of the bar. Through the doorway behind, an unused corner of a room. The vial stands on a small hallway shelf in the near foreground, sharp and lit.

Editorial, photoreal, real environment with depth and context. Composition is deliberately top-weighted: the subject and all detail sit in the upper two thirds. The lower third of the frame falls away into deep unlit shadow and plain uninterrupted surface with no objects, no texture detail and no highlights. Natural window light from above. Not a studio packshot on slate.

PRODUCT (reproduce EXACTLY as the reference images show; re-light it to this scene, never paste it flat): small injectable glass vial, black rubber cap + gold metal band. Container/source ref: `Dialed Health Injectable.png`

LOCKED: Label = logo + product name only. No dosing text, no extra copy — locked since the first vial generation.
LOCKED: Never composite / paste product renders into scenes — always regenerate in-scene with references (house-wide rule; composites read as photoshopped).
LOCKED: Label artwork is sacred in lifestyle shots — it must come EXACTLY from the approved studio shot reference; the model must re-light it to the scene, never invent new text.
LOCKED: Vial upright and vertical in hand-held shots — tilting is what wrecks label fidelity.
LOCKED: Realistic scale — the vial is tiny (~2/3 the length of an index finger); oversized vials were rejected.
LOCKED: Motion blur rule (evolved, current preference): CAMERA-IN-MOTION full-frame blur , not limb-localized. (The older rule — blur must come from a visibly moving limb, never sprinkled on a static pose — still holds as the floor: static-pose sprinkled blur is always wrong.)
